Projects shall strengthen the institutional capacity of local governments for resilience development and management, including through targeted training that improves staff competences in modern development standards and ensure access to essential citizen-centred public services.
 Common values and principles: Project Promoters, Partners and projects shall respect the values and principles governing the implementation of the Norwegian Financial Mechanism, as referred to in Article 1.3.1 of the Regulation, i.e. human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and the respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. Applicants shall describe how gender equality considerations are integrated into the project.
 The strategic role and polycentrism: the call is addressed to cities that perform central functions of national and regional significance in Polish polycentric  network. Its objective is to strengthen the capacity of cities to prevent and withstand threats, respond effectively to crisis situations, and adapt to changing social, economic, environmental, and security conditions. As a general rule, solutions relating to safety and resilience will be developed and tested in larger centres so that the resulting solutions can be recommended to towns with less administrative capacity. In addition, the call aims to leverage the potential of regional cities to develop model resilience initiatives that can subsequently be replicated and implemented in other, smaller urban area. 
 Thematic scope of projects: Enhancement of the resilience of Polish cities will be provided by supporting the development and implementation of integrated, pilot solutions that strengthen preparedness for a wide range of natural, technological and militarian hazards. The call promotes embedding resilience into urban governance, planning, and crisis management in line with national, European, and international frameworks.
 This call aims to identify and support initiatives that improve urban capacities across the emergency management cycle, with a particular focus on prevention and preparedness. Actions supported under the call should apply an all-hazards and whole-of-society approach, fostering cooperation between local authorities, emergency services, civil society, the private sector, and residents.
 The call will prioritize projects with a holistic, cross-sectoral approach that brings together a wide range of stakeholders. This is reflected in the assessment criteria, which reward projects that are based on a robust diagnosis of local challenges; are composed of combination of different activities, are operationally linked to crisis management plans and other relevant strategic documents and include relevant stakeholder groups (including civil society organisations).
 The projects can implement the activities from the seven thematic areas:
- Developing alert and warning systems. 
- Monitor environmental and other risks by using Internet of Things (IoT) solutions. 
- Improving infrastructure, equipment, and management of the crisis centres in the cities. 
- Critical infrastructure protection, including alternative methods of water and energy supply. 
- Use of geospatial information system (GIS) for urban risk monitoring and analysis.  
- Modernisation and development of protective structures and storage facilities. 
- Information integrity.

Purpose of this call is to enable umbrella organisations to pursue their own long term goals and missions. Organisational Grants provide multiannual, flexible financial support based on the organisation’s existing strategic or organisational work plan, funding both capacity building and core activities essential to fulfilling their role within the sector.
 Eligible Applicants
 Project promoters must be Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) established in Portugal, operating as non-profit, voluntary and private entities, irrespective of their legal form, and complying with the following requirements at the time of application submission:
 a) is established as a legal entity;
 b) pursues the general interest or common good and has a non-commercial purpose;
 c) is independent of local, regional and central government, public entities, political parties and commercial organisations;
 d) is not a political organisation or a political party;
 e) is not a religious institution.
 In addition to the stated conditions, promoters submitting an application to this call must be an umbrella organisation established in Portugal. For the purposes of this call notice, an umbrella organisation is a legally established entity that represents, coordinates, or provides services to a network, federation, or association of multiple independent member organisations operating within a common sector, theme, or purpose relevant to the Fund. The organisation shall cumulatively: 
 a) Have a mission that aligns with the Fund’s areas of support, as defined in the Fund rules;
 b) Have a formal membership base comprising at least five distinct legal entities, the majority of which must be non-governmental organisations;
 c) Be able to demonstrate that its activities primarily serve and benefit its member organisations;
 d) Be registered and compliant with applicable legal and regulatory requirements;
 e) Be able to demonstrate previous work with the Fund’s areas of support and a membership base comprising of at least 60 % active member organisations with a primary statutory purpose that falls within one or more of the Programmes areas of support: 
 i. promoting civic participation in democratic processes;
 ii. promoting information integrity and media literacy;
 iii. protecting human rights, including antidiscrimination and social justice;
 iv. promoting gender equality, including SRHR (Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights) and LGBTIQ+ rights;
 v. promoting climate action, environmental protection, and just green transition;
 f) Have a multiannual work plan and/or strategy;
 g) Have been legally registered for at least 48 months prior to the submission deadline;  
 h) Demonstrate an average annual turnover over the last three completed financial years of at least twice the annualised value of the grant amount applied for;
 i) Be in compliance with its payment obligations regarding taxes and social security.

data.aim: The genetic diversity of cultivated plants and farm animals is a cornerstone for the development of more resilient, economically viable, and environmentally sustainable production systems. The agroecological transition largely relies on farmers’ access to new species, varieties, and breeds that can support the redesign of their farming systems and evolution towards agroecology. Moreover, farmers’ motivations and capacities to engage in the agroecological transition strongly depend on social and behavourial factors, including their skills and knowledge, their personal characteristics and those of their farms, as well as the support provided by advisory systems and public policies.

The second topic addresses the social challenges of today’s agriculture, with a particular focus on farmers' motivation, skills, and knowledge and the role of stakeholders in encouraging their engagement in the agroecological transition.

data.desc: What are Growth Projects?  BASS Growth Projects are a new funding framework designed to help space-enabled solutions that have already achieved demonstrable commercial success in a primary market to unlock secondary market opportunities.  The scope of Growth Projects includes the development, integration and testing of new service elements to meet the requirements of secondary markets, as well as the implementation of large-scale pilots.  Who are Growth Projects for? ESA BASS Growth Projects are aimed at ambitious companies or industrial teams which have developed a space-enabled solution that has already been validated in the primary market. This funding opportunity is intended as a springboard for business growth by supporting expansion into new markets.  What we offer   ESA funding personalised support from a member of the ESA team  the use of the ESA brand for credibility Optional Support: Some companies applying for Growth Projects may not yet have a fully established ecosystem to commercialise their solution at scale and may need to expand their network of partners. For this reason, the Growth Project framework offers optional support to assist companies with establishing strategic partnerships, expanding the value chain, enabling access to global markets and managing the business risks associated with the identified market opportunities. This will be done by connecting applicants with strategic players from the Growth Projects Partner Network. This network, established by ESA, brings together business multipliers, investors, accelerators, consultancies, users, customers, and data or asset providers, with the objective of fostering strategic partnerships that strengthen the value chain, facilitate access to global markets, and mitigate business risks by connecting projects with organisations able to provide relevant expertise, resources, or market access.  If your company can provide some of the support described above, scroll further down for more information. The optional support includes access to: the Growth Projects Partner Network ESA BASS Task Forces business coaching, matchmaking and exposure opportunities networking and dedicated events How much funding is available? Please see the detailed co-funding rules below:   Growth Projects Activity Cost case by case assessment (limited to eligible cost) ESA Co-funding   Baseline up to 50% of eligible cost Micro, small and medium enterprises up to 80% of eligible cost Universities, research institutes, the public sector (without commercial interest) up to 100% of eligible cost with ESA co-funding not exceeding 30% of the total activity cost Universities, research institutes, the public sector (with commercial interest) up to 75% of eligible cost Industry co-funding remaining costs required to carry out the activity. Co-funding can be provided through the public or private sector, directly or indirectly Please note that funding participation is open to groups, organisations and businesses that reside in ESA member states that have subscribed to BASS. Currently these countries are Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. How to apply for a Growth Project To start the application process you will first need to create an account on ESA's Open Space Innovation Platform (OSIP). The application process follows a standard three-step process: Growth Project Questionnaire (GPQ) > Outline Proposal > Full Proposal Within the GPQ form, the company can indicate areas of support required at the point of submission. Once the GPQ step has successfully passed to the next stage, ESA will support when possible by, for example, facilitating introductions with members of the Growth Projects Partner Network.  Please note that a Written Authorisation for ESA Funding must be submitted together with the Full Proposal – applicants are advised to contact their National Delegation(s) as early as possible in the process to obtain one. data.desc: The Opportunity   Tourism is one of Europe's most important economic sectors, contributing significantly to employment, regional development and economic growth. Following the recovery of international travel since COVID-19, destinations across Europe are experiencing increasing visitor numbers while facing growing pressure to manage tourism sustainably, enhance visitor experiences and protect natural and cultural assets.  Destinations, tourism operators and public authorities are looking for innovative digital solutions that support more efficient tourism management, improve visitor services and help balance economic growth with environmental and social sustainability. Challenges such as overtourism, seasonal demand fluctuations, congestion, accessibility, environmental impact and changing traveller expectations require new approaches supported by reliable data and real-time insights.  At the same time, visitors increasingly expect personalised, seamless and digital experiences before, during and after their trips. Meanwhile, tourism stakeholders require better tools to understand visitor flows, monitor destinations, optimise infrastructure, improve safety and support informed decision-making.  Topics of relevance  Visitor flow monitoring and management  Services that monitor and forecast visitor movements, identify congestion and help distribute visitors more effectively. Solutions could include dynamic routing, congestion alerts and decision-support tools for destination managers.   Sustainable tourism and environmental monitoring  Solutions that help destinations and tourism operators assess and reduce their environmental impact. Applications could include monitoring environmental pressures, land-use or coastal changes and emissions, as well as supporting sustainability reporting, responsible destination planning and regenerative tourism models.   Smart cultural and natural heritage management  Services supporting the monitoring and protection of cultural and natural heritage sites. Applications could include site-condition assessment, risk detection, visitor-impact analysis and digital models supporting conservation and long-term asset management.   Seamless mobility and travel experience  Integrated services that make it easier for visitors to combine different transport modes, particularly when accessing rural, remote or less-connected destinations. Applications could include multimodal travel planning, accessibility routing and improved first- and last-mile connectivity.   Immersive and inclusive tourism experiences  Location-based digital services that improve access to cultural and natural assets. These could include augmented and virtual reality experiences, accessible navigation for people with disabilities, digital interpretation tools and remote tourism experiences.   Safety, resilience and crisis support  Services helping travellers, tourism operators and destinations respond to natural hazards, environmental events and operational disruptions. Applications could include situational awareness, location-based alerts, emergency communications and crisis decision-support tools.   Remote connectivity for rural and remote destinations  Connectivity solutions enabling tourism services in areas with limited terrestrial coverage. Applications could support rural tourism businesses, online bookings, digital guest services, Internet of Things monitoring and access to real-time travel and safety information.  Value of Space  Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS)  GNSS can provide precise positioning for visitor flow analysis, navigation, mobility services and accessible routing. It can support the monitoring of visitor movements, helping tourism destinations understand how visitors move between locations, and manage visitor flows more effectively. GNSS can also enable location-based tourism experiences, including digital services that provide information or content according to the visitor’s location. Geofencing, tracking and safety functions can further support visitor management and improve mobility across tourism destinations.   Satellite Earth Observation (SatEO)  SatEO can provide data for environmental monitoring, land-use and coastal-change detection, and the assessment of natural and cultural assets. It can support destinations and tourism operators in monitoring environmental pressures associated with tourism activities and understanding changes affecting sensitive locations. SatEO can also contribute to sustainability indicators, environmental impact assessments and evidence-based destination planning. These capabilities can support the protection and long-term management of natural and cultural heritage, as well as the development of more sustainable and responsible tourism.   Satellite Communications (SatCom)  SatCom can provide connectivity in remote or poorly served areas where terrestrial infrastructure may be insufficient. This can enable digital services for travellers and tourism businesses, including online bookings, digital guest services and access to real-time travel and safety information. SatCom can also support IoT monitoring networks, emergency communications and remote access to digital content. By providing connectivity where terrestrial services are limited or disrupted, SatCom can contribute to the operational continuity and resilience of tourism services in rural, peripheral and hard-to-reach destinations.  What we look for We invite submissions of early-stage service concepts that address customer needs, show commercial potential and technical feasibility, and leverage satellite data or space technology. Kick-starts should be led by experienced, motivated teams, with a clear ambition and a credible pathway to developing commercially viable services. What we offer We offer funding and support to companies, specifically to help teams carry out a feasibility study over a six-month period. During this time, teams can develop their business case, work on technical aspects, validating the integration of satellite data and space technologies into the proposed solution, and engage actively with users and customers.  We offer:  75% funding from the European Space Agency to a maximum of €75,000 for each selected study, provided on a zero-equity basis. The total cost per study is up to €100,000.  Technical and commercial guidance  Access to our network and partners  Use of the ESA brand for your service  Please note that we do not provide direct access to space data, nor are we responsible for the space segment of service development. Applicants should have a clear plan for how they will obtain any required space data and ensure they have the necessary expertise within their team to help manage this aspect.  Who can apply? data.desc: The funding opportunity Road and traffic safety is a critical concern globally. In many regions, rapid urbanisation and the growing number of vehicles have led to increased accidents, amplifying the need for improved traffic management, incident detection, and predictive safety solutions to reduce accidents, injuries, and fatalities on the roads. Also, there is a change in the types of vehicles we see on roads, with increasing presence of micromobility and automated vehicles reshaping existing mobility patterns. These emerging modes of transport require updated safety solutions to ensure that traffic management and infrastructure are adapted accordingly. This opportunity offers funding for teams who would like to develop sustainable space-based services and applications that address challenges related to the Road and Traffic Safety sector. The challenge According to the World Health Organization (WHO), approximately 1.35 million people die each year because of road traffic crashes, making it the leading cause of death for children and young adults aged 5-29 years. In September 2020, the UN General Assembly proclaimed the Decade of Action for Road Safety, with the ambitious target of preventing at least 50% of road traffic deaths and injuries by 2030. European governments continue to monitor progress towards this target, regularly updating standards and encouraging the ‘safety first’ mentality such as the use of seat belts and helmets.  Industry is also actively working on improving safety of both vehicles and the surrounding ecosystem. With the rise of digital, connected and autonomous mobility solutions, there is enormous potential for improved safety through reduced human error and improved information sharing. New services at the intersection of these trends have the potential to drastically improve the safety of roads and bring scalable benefits. The market is projected to grow, driven by advancements in artificial intelligence, IoT sensors and cloud computing, allowing for greater accuracy, scalability and cost-effectiveness of road safety systems. Against this backdrop of increasing risks, evolving mobility patterns and expanding technological opportunities, this proposed Road and Traffic Safety Call for Proposals aims to develop solutions that leverage space-enabled technologies to enhance safety and traffic management, to improve the collection of critical data, and to better protect vulnerable road users, ultimately contributing to the reduction of accidents, injuries, and fatalities on the roads. Topics of relevance This Call for Proposals has been designed in collaboration with ESA BASS partners, who have helped to identify the following use cases. Please note, that these are only examples and the call is not limited to the use cases listed below: Enhancing information exchange Vehicle-to-Vehicle and Vehicle-to-Infrastructure communication applications could allow vehicles to share information about their speed, position and direction, as well as providing alerts about potential dangers, such as approaching vehicles or hazardous road conditions. This near real-time data exchange can enhance overall road safety of passengers, drivers, cyclists and pedestrians. Improving Road design, signage and maintenance to reduce accidents Well-designed roads with clear signage and better road markings can help drivers navigate safely and support automated vehicles by ensuring they have the necessary references. Regular and proactive road maintenance such as repairing potholes, clearing debris, restoring worn markings, and addressing drainage issues prevents accidents caused by deteriorating road conditions. It can be achieved through:  Rapid detection, prioritisation and repair of road defects, such as potholes, surface cracks, faded markings, or obstructed signage. Designing and planning safer infrastructure to address the needs of pedestrians, cyclists, motorcyclists and paying attention to the specific needs of people with disabilities, children and the elderly. Upgrading existing infrastructure for improved prevention, detection and communication of accidents.  Improving road safety by optimising traffic flow Validation of environmental claims, cross-validation of data and validation of inconsistencies for insurance companies, auditing firms, certifying bodies and corporations. Monitoring traffic flow and congestion helps to identify bottlenecks and areas with high accident rates and allows for dynamic adjustments to traffic signals and other control measures. This can improve the overall efficiency and safety of the road network by reducing traffic jams and alleviating congestion during peak hours. Implementing measures to protect non-motorised road users Implementing measures to protect non-motorised road users and to ensure that pedestrians, micromobility users and cyclists have safe spaces to travel, reducing the risk of accidents. Such measures could involve systems monitoring vulnerable road users' safety and providing alerts about potential dangers, such as approaching vehicles or hazardous road conditions. Improving International Road Assessment Programme (iRAP) survey completion The star-rating protocol, set out by the International Road Assessment Programme (iRAP), is a way to assess how safe roads are. These surveys rely on information about road context, observed traffic flow, and infrastructure attributes to produce risk-based safety ratings. Tools to significantly improve the completion of surveys, through increasing cost-effectiveness, efficiency, frequency and precision are needed. Value of space SatEO imagery can be used to update maps, monitor environmental hazards, and assess the conditions of roads. SatEO is valuable for planning and maintaining road networks, therefore preventing accidents caused by poor road conditions. SatEO data, such as weather nowcasting, can help vehicle systems to adjust the vehicle's speed and trajectory to current road conditions. Finally, SatEO can be used in advanced routing applications to optimise the route based on hazards or weather conditions. SatNav provides accurate positioning, navigation, and timing, which are essential for guiding and navigating vehicles, especially those with autonomous capabilities.  Aggregated GNSS data from connected vehicles, fleets, and mobile devices can be used to monitor traffic flow and to identify congestion patterns. This can improve the overall safety of the road network by reducing traffic jams and congestion during peak hours. SatCom can ensure seamless communication between various systems, enabling near real-time data exchange and coordination.  Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) and Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) communication can leverage Satcom to ensure seamless connectivity in remote areas, therefore playing a significant role in detecting and communicating information about potential hazards. Who can apply? This opportunity is open to companies that intend to develop space-enabled services and products related, but not restricted, to the topics of relevance outlined above.   To be eligible for funding, your team must be based in one of the following countries: Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and United Kingdom. data.desc: The Opportunity ESA Business Applications and Space Solutions (BASS) is launching a Contest to connect companies developing space-enabled services with leading industry challenge owners. The call focuses on specific operational and innovation needs identified by Coca-Cola, P&G, Galp and Tomorrowland/Love Tomorrow across water resilience, security and enterprise risk, renewable energy, sustainable manufacturing, consumer insight, temporary-city operations, mobility, logistics and immersive experiences. The Contest offers companies a unique opportunity to rapidly prototype and validate their solutions with leading industrial organisations acting as both challenge owners and potential prospective customers. Winning teams will gain direct access to participating corporate partners to test their solution against real operational needs and accelerate the path towards commercial adoption. The Challenges Applicants are invited to respond the published challenges specified by by Coca-Cola, P&G, Galp and Tomorrowland/Love Tomorrow by proposing a six-month Proof-of-concept Study. The challenge topics include but are not limited to: water resilience environmental stewardship digital twins immersive experiences sustainable logistics and supply chains consumer insights Follow the steps in the How To Apply section to access the full list of challenges. If you are planning on applying, please be sure to contact your National Delegation at your earliest convenience, as you will require written authorisation from them to benefit from this funding. Value of Space Earth observation can provide wide-area, repeatable and independent information on water availability, drought, dust transport, land use, vegetation, biodiversity, infrastructure condition, natural hazards, facility access, transport corridors and environmental change. Commercial and Copernicus data may be combined with non-space datasets, AI, change detection and predictive analytics to turn observations into decision-ready services. Satellite navigation can support positioning, tracking, geolocation and time-referenced analysis of people, vehicles, assets, infrastructure, observations and interventions. This is relevant to mobility and logistics, renewable-asset operations, temporary-city management and location-aware experiences. Satellite communications and hybrid connectivity can connect remote, mobile or temporary sensors and assets, provide resilient backhaul, and support operational access where terrestrial connectivity is limited, disrupted or congested. Space-derived technologies and expertise developed for human monitoring, closed-loop life-support, water recovery, resource-efficient processing, digital twins and constrained operations may also be transferred to consumer insight and sustainable manufacturing challenges.   Who can apply? To be eligible for funding, your team must be based in one of the following countries: Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and United Kingdom.   Potential Tenderers are strongly advised to contact the National Delegation(s) of the countries where their industrial partners (Prime and Subcontractors) are located as soon as possible.  A Written Authorisation for ESA funding from the National Delegation(s) is required for the Full Proposal.  The activity should build on a credible technical starting point, integrate relevant space assets, and test the most important technical, operational and business assumptions through a focused Proof-of-concept. Solutions should provide clear value to the challenge owner while showing potential for repeatability, wider market adoption or further commercialisation. Application process This is a competitive funding call, for which applicants will need to submit a Full Proposal. Following evaluation, selected applicants will be invited to pitch their solution to a jury, including representatives from ESA and the corporate challenge owners. Winning teams will be offered a Cooperative Agreement to implement the proposed Proof-of-concept Study. data.desc: The Opportunity The Smart and Resilient Energy Systems Call for Proposals aims to develop operational solutions using space-enabled technologies to improve the anticipatory, operational, and strategic resilience of electricity grids. Solutions should have a strong focus on critical infrastructure protection, climate resilience, and emergency preparedness. The Call has been developed in collaboration with ELES, Slovenia's combined transmission and distribution system operator, and is based on operational requirements and challenges identified by the organisation. These requirements reflect real-world needs associated with forecasting and grid operations, dynamic thermal rating enhancement, asset intelligence, infrastructure monitoring, digital twin integration and situational awareness across electricity networks, and form the foundation for the use cases within this call. This Call for Proposals will accept proposals for Proof-of-Concept Studies and Pilot Projects. Topics of relevance This Call addresses operational challenges identified by ELES and is organised into three complementary solution clusters. Cluster A: Forecasting & Grid Operations Modern electricity networks require increasingly sophisticated forecasting, planning and operational decision-support capabilities to support network stability, renewable integration and resilient system operation. Areas of interest include: Renewable generation forecasting for solar and wind power Load-flow prediction and congestion analysis Contingency planning for unplanned outages Cross-border scheduling and balancing coordination Seasonal and long-term capacity planning Climate and weather risk assessment Strategic outage mitigation planning Solutions should improve operational awareness, forecasting accuracy and decision-support capabilities across transmission and distribution networks while supporting efficient network utilisation and improved resilience. Cluster B: Dynamic Thermal Rating Enhancement ELES operates the SUMO Dynamic Thermal Rating (DTR) system and is seeking improved environmental monitoring and forecasting capabilities to enhance the utilisation of existing transmission infrastructure. Areas of interest include: Enhanced wind speed and wind direction monitoring Ambient temperature and solar irradiance monitoring High-resolution nowcasting and forecasting of environmental parameters at conductor-representative heights Historical environmental analysis and weather model calibration Integration of environmental data into the SUMO DTR system and operational workflows Solutions should improve the spatial resolution, accuracy and timeliness of environmental inputs to Dynamic Thermal Rating calculations, particularly across Alpine and pre-Alpine transmission corridors. Cluster C: Asset Intelligence, Digital Twin & Situational Awareness Electricity network operators require improved visibility of infrastructure condition, environmental threats and operational risks to support effective asset management and resilient network operations. Areas of interest include: Predictive maintenance and anomaly detection Asset prioritisation and vulnerability assessment Digital twin enrichment and automated data integration Natural hazard monitoring Infrastructure condition monitoring Emergency situational awareness Obstacle and encroachment detection Vegetation and corridor monitoring Cross-domain resilience dashboards Smart-grid assessment and future operational planning Solutions should integrate Earth Observation, Artificial Intelligence, advanced analytics and digital-twin capabilities to improve asset intelligence, infrastructure monitoring and operational awareness across the electricity network. Value of Space Space enabled services can significantly enhance electricity grid operations across multiple domains: Satellite Earth Observation (SatEO) enables large-scale, near-real-time or latency-dependent monitoring of hazards such as floods, storms, wildfires, landslides, snow and icing events, as well as vegetation encroachment, construction activities and asset surroundings. These capabilities complement local inspections, drone operations, and GIS-based monitoring, while improving crisis awareness, emergency response coordination and long-term climate resilience planning. When combined with advanced analytics and AI techniques, EO data can also support predictive maintenance, asset prioritisation and digital-twin enrichment, enabling a shift from reactive to risk-based operations. Satellite Communications (SatCom) enables ubiquitous connectivity to enhance communication links, connectivity of IoT devices and networks of sensors, in remote locations. SatCom also provides real-time, long-range communications with infrastructure monitoring systems (i.e. UAVs/robots), enabling remote operation while assisting enabling technologies such as digital twins. Satellite Navigation (SatNav) supports precise asset localisation, time synchronisation for digital operational systems and secure backup communications during emergency or degraded terrestrial network conditions. These services can enhance operational continuity and coordination during large-scale disruptions or crisis events. Satellite enhanced forecasting improves the spatial and temporal resolution of weather driven inputs (solar irradiance, wind fields, ambient temperature), directly supporting renewable generation forecasting, load flow prediction, and dynamic thermal rating. What we are looking for  We look for motivated teams with established business, financial and technical expertise who can address our focus areas with market-ready concepts. Submitted proposals must demonstrate:  Commercial Viability and Sustainable Business Models: Service concepts designed for long-term commercial profitability. Projects targeting public sector or law enforcement users (B2G) are strongly encouraged to incorporate commercial B2B customer streams to ensure post-project sustainability.  Operational Readiness over Research: A clear focus on deploying pre-operational commercial services rather than pure academic research or basic scientific data exploration. Concepts must be driven by practical market demand and active user support.  Technical Data Self-Sufficiency: Bidding teams must already possess the internal technical capability to acquire and process downstream space data. Teams must be self-sufficient from the outset, as ESA provides financial and strategic backing rather than direct software engineering support.  Distinct Space Added Value: Clear, measurable operational or commercial advantages derived directly from the integration of space assets over traditional terrestrial alternatives.  What we offer  Zero-equity co-funding: up to 50–80% of your activity costs, depending on SME status and Member State approval.  Technical and commercial guidance  Access to our network, partners and Taskforce members  ESA brand credibility  Who can apply? Entities residing in Slovenia do not need to provide dedicated Letters of Authorisation from their National Delegation, subject to the conditions stated in the attached Authorisation of Funding (AoF). For companies based in Denmark, please note that the conditions and timeline specified in the Authorisation of Funding (AoF), available under the “Who can apply?” section of the “Open Call for Proposals: Proof-of-concept Studies and Pilot Projects”, apply and take precedence over the information provided in this page. How to apply  Visit the How to Apply to Proof-of-concept studies and Pilot Projects page for the full application details.  The call opens for submissions on 29 September 2026 and closes on 27 November 2026. This closing date refers strictly to the deadline for submitting the initial Activity Pitch Questionnaire (APQ) via the Open Space Innovation Platform (OSIP). Introduction This is part of the Wildfire Safety initiative, inviting proposals for innovative services that advance wildfire management using space technology and data. The first call focused on Wildfire Response, supporting solutions for early detection of wildfires, near-real-time fire evolution monitoring, and fire behaviour simulation and prediction. Challenges Wildfires have forever played an integral role in regulating our natural environment; shaping landscapes and sustaining ecosystems. However, in recent years, the frequency and intensity of wildfires in Europe’s Southern Mediterranean region, as well as parts of Central and Eastern Europe, have notably increased. Data from the European Forest Fires Information System (EFFIS) suggests that the average area affected by fires in 2025 in European Union member states was more than double the average from across 2006-2024. Human activity and environmental conditions favouring wildfire ignition and propagation have historically been the catalysts behind such fires. The extension of urban-forest interfaces, where human settlements and flammable vegetation meet, is exacerbating both the risk of fire onset and the magnitude of their impact. The consequences of such are environmental, economic and social. Wildfires cause extensive loss of, and damage to, lives, natural resources, and property. Local economies suffer due to impacts on tourism, abandonment of rural areas and disruption of trade. The burning of biomass releases pollutants negatively impacting air quality and sowing longer-term impacts on human health and the environment. In parallel, on-going advances in space and terrestrial technologies offer novel means to tackle such challenges. Satellite Earth observation for mapping and monitoring of active fires, burn scars, vegetative health, risk factors, vulnerable infrastructure, and otherwise. Satellite communications to provide connectivity to distributed in-situ sensors across a region, as well as communication links for aerial platforms. data.title: The Arctic Region
data.desc: The Arctic, the most northerly region on Earth, is centred on the North Pole and defined as the area North of the Arctic Circle, 66°N. It is known for its polar night, extensive sea ice, tundra landscape, polar climate and cold adapted ecosystems. It is a region that is also disproportionately impacted by climate change, warming three to four times faster than the global average. The melting ice has led to the Arctic becoming a strategic security zone, as competing global powers vie for control of newly accessible shipping routes and abundant natural resources including oil, gas and rare-earth minerals. Rapid snowmelt threatens towns, roads and industrial infrastructure with flooding, while so-called ‘zombie’ or overwintering wildfires burn year-round in the carbon-rich peat, undetected for extensive periods of time before re-emerging to the surface. Thawing permafrost causes land subsidence, destabilising buildings and releasing greenhouse gases, pollutants and pathogens. The diverse threats facing the Arctic environment, livelihoods, security and economy are expected to become more consequential over time. There is a pressing need to develop solutions to address current and emerging challenges. From maritime safety and surveillance, to search and rescue, defence and security, environmental protection, food security and critical infrastructure protection, the potential for using satellite technologies in innovative solutions is immense. Structure of the Arctic call To address the diversity and complexity of the challenges affecting the Arctic region, this Call for Proposals is composed of three complementary and thematically focused sub‑calls. Each sub‑call targets a specific set of user needs and operational challenges, while sharing a common objective: supporting the development of space‑enabled services that enhance resilience, safety, sustainability and security in the Arctic region. The three sub‑calls are designed to be distinct yet interconnected, reflecting the tight interplay between environmental change, economic activity, maritime operations and geopolitical dynamics. Applicants are encouraged to focus on the sub‑call that best matches their use case and user community. Sub‑call 1 – Environmental and economic resilience This call is now open and closes 4 September 2026 This sub‑call focuses on protecting Arctic ecosystems and supporting climate‑resilient economic activities, with particular attention to fisheries, aquaculture, environmental monitoring, pollution detection and food security. It addresses the growing impact of climate change, increased maritime activity and environmental stressors on both Arctic livelihoods and natural resources. Sub‑call 2 – Safety, navigation and operations This call opens 5 September 2026 and closes 5 November 2026 This sub‑call targets safe maritime navigation and operations in the Arctic, where melting sea ice is not only increasing traffic but also exposing vessels to significant hazards. It addresses challenges related to ice monitoring, route optimisation, search and rescue, situational awareness, and the safe operation of maritime, air and land activities in a remote and infrastructure‑limited environment. Sub‑call 3 – Security and critical protection This call opens 6 November 2026 and closes 6 January 2027 This sub‑call addresses security, sovereignty and protection of critical infrastructure in an increasingly contested region. It focuses on enhancing situational awareness, monitoring unlawful and grey‑zone activities, protecting strategic assets, and supporting Arctic states and allies in responding to growing geopolitical and hybrid threats. What we look for We look for promising business ideas addressing topics of relevance or related areas that propose: attractive market opportunities, identified customer needs and customer engagement commercially-viable service concepts technically feasible solutions added value of space data or technology motivated teams with business, technical and financial expertise What we offer We offer funding and support to companies, both for business case assessment and for the development of new, space-based services. data.countryText: Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and United Kingdom
data.desc: The Opportunity   As energy systems face growing operational, environmental and security challenges, ensuring the resilience of Europe's electricity grids is becoming increasingly important. This is driving demand for innovative solutions that can help grid operators anticipate, detect and respond to disruptions, while maintaining a secure and reliable energy supply.  This Call for Proposals is conducted in collaboration with ENTSO-E, the European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity. As part of ESA’s Task Force for Innovation in Energy Through Space, ENTSO-E has consolidated a representative set of generic operational challenges for electricity transmission networks, focusing on system operation, resilience, situational awareness and operational efficiency. The Call invites proposals for Proof-of-concept Studies and Pilot Projects for services addressing selected challenges relevant to the resilience and operational continuity of European electricity transmission systems. These include:  growing physical, cyber, and climate-related risks​ to energy infrastructure  increasingly extreme weather events (such as wildfires, floods, storms, heatwaves) affecting grid operations​   increasing dependency on secure infrastructure​ for digitalisation and interconnected power systems, and  economic, societal, and national security impacts from disruption to energy systems  The challenges have been identified through engagement with ENTSO-E and European Transmission System Operators. They are illustrative, intentionally generalised and intended to stimulate innovation. They should not be interpreted as descriptions of the current operational practices, existing capability gaps or specific priorities of ENTSO-E or any individual TSO. Subject to their individual interest and applicable internal, operational, security, regulatory and procurement requirements, participating TSOs may engage with selected bidders as potential users and contribute to the validation and demonstration of proposed solutions. The involvement of ENTSO-E and/or individual TSOs in the development of the thematic scope, use cases, consultations or other activities associated with this Call does not constitute an endorsement, certification, commitment to participate in a pilot, commitment to procure or purchase any solution, or any other contractual or commercial commitment. Any future participation, testing, procurement or deployment by an individual TSO will be subject to its own decision-making processes, applicable legal, regulatory, security, operational and procurement requirements. Topics of Relevance  The use cases are organised under two complementary challenge areas, reflecting the operational needs identified by ENTSO-E in relation to the secure and resilient operation of Europe's interconnected electricity transmission system.  The proposed activities build on existing space-enabled capabilities and services, including Earth observation, positioning, navigation and timing, and satellite communications. The objective is therefore not to develop these capabilities in isolation, but to demonstrate their operational value for TSOs and explore how they can complement existing terrestrial solutions, strengthen resilience and support continuity of grid operations.  The two themes will open for applications one after the other: Theme 1 applications are invited from November 4 2026 to January 29 2027, Theme 2 applications will be invited from February 1 2027 to 30 April 2027. Theme 1 | Situational Awareness for Critical Events  | Opening: 2.11.2026 | Closing: 29.01.2027 Developing solutions that improve the ability of Transmission System Operators to anticipate, detect, understand and assess risks affecting electricity transmission infrastructure and system stability through enhanced awareness of environmental hazards, infrastructure condition and evolving operational risks. Key capabilities:​   Early detection and monitoring of wildfires, floods, extreme weather, and infrastructure failures​  Monitoring of transmission corridors, vegetation encroachment, and environmental risks​  Integration of space weather information for grid risk forecasting​  Post-event damage assessment and operational recovery support​  Scalable and interoperable platforms supporting use across multiple transmission system environments, subject to applicable requirements Theme 2 | Strengthening Operational Resilience for the Grid | Opening: 1.2.2027 | Closing: 30.4.2027 Enhancing the resilience, security and continuity of grid operations through improved operational capabilities, communications, positioning, timing and emergency response services that support effective operation during normal and degraded conditions. Key capabilities:​   High-accuracy and resilient timing capabilities for applications within digital substations and other grid applications requiring stringent timing performance, subject to applicable technical and security requirements ​   Precise positioning for onshore and offshore grid assets​   Detection of interference, spoofing, and signal degradation​   Satellite backup communications when terrestrial networks fail​   Secure connectivity for grid restoration and emergency operations     Value of Space  Space assets provide critical capabilities to support grid resilience:​   Satellite Earth Observation (SatEO) data can provide valuable capabilities for monitoring infrastructure, environmental risks and to assess damage.   SatEO provides wide-area, persistent monitoring of transmission corridors and substations, enabling near real-time detection and forecasting of wildfires, and supporting rapid flood mapping and post-event damage assessment. SatEO also allows operators to monitor vegetation  encroachment and construction activities that may impact the grid and to detect ground deformation using radar techniques, identifying subsidence or structural movements that could affect critical infrastructure.     Satellite Navigation (SatNav) can provide high-precision positioning capabilities that may support applications within digital sub-stations and other grid assets requiring a stringent synchronisation performance. SatNav can also enable the detection of structural displacement or slow asset movement, and provides independent, resilient timing sources that migrate risks associated with terrestrial timing failures or signal interference.      Satellite Communications (SatCom) support secure and resilient connectivity during outages and emergencies.  SatCom can provide secure backup connectivity during terrestrial network outages or cyber incidents, and enable rapid deployment of communications in disaster-affected areas. It also supports independent command-and-control channels for grid restoration operations, and may support resilient backup communications and interoperability with relevant utility communication environments, subject to the applicable technical, cybersecurity and operational requirements.    Space Weather services can provide valuable capabilities for forecasting and monitoring solar and geomagnetic activity that may impact electricity transmission systems. Space Weather services support the prediction of geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) and provide early warning of severe geomagnetic disturbances that may affect grid infrastructure. These capabilities can help operators improve situational awareness, assess potential impacts on critical assets, and support preparedness and mitigation activities before and during space weather events.   Supporting digital technologies including  Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Digital Twins, and advanced data fusion and analytics. What we are looking for  We look for motivated teams with established business, financial and technical expertise who can address our focus areas with market-ready concepts. Submitted proposals must demonstrate:  Commercial Viability and Sustainable Business Models: Service concepts designed for long-term commercial profitability. Projects targeting public sector or law enforcement users (B2G) are strongly encouraged to incorporate commercial B2B customer streams to ensure post-project sustainability.  Operational Readiness over Research: A clear focus on deploying pre-operational commercial services rather than pure academic research or basic scientific data exploration. Concepts must be driven by practical market demand and active user support.  Technical Data Self-Sufficiency: Bidding teams must already possess the internal technical capability to acquire and process downstream space data. Teams must be self-sufficient from the outset, as ESA provides financial and strategic backing rather than direct software engineering support.  Distinct Space Added Value: Clear, measurable operational or commercial advantages derived directly from the integration of space assets over traditional terrestrial alternatives.  What we offer  Zero-equity co-funding: up to 50–80% of your activity costs, depending on SME status and Member State approval.  Technical and commercial guidance  Access to our network, partners and Taskforce members  ESA brand credibility  Who can apply? To be eligible for funding, your team must be based in one of the following countries: Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and United Kingdom.   Potential Tenderers are strongly advised to contact the National Delegation(s) of the countries where their industrial partners (Prime and Subcontractors) are located as soon as possible.  A Written Authorisation for ESA funding from the National Delegation(s) is required for the Full Proposal.  How to apply  Visit the How to Apply to Proof-of-concept studies and Pilot Projects page for the full application details.  Proposals are assessed individually on a rolling, non-competitive basis; companies are therefore strongly encouraged to submit their APQ as early as possible.  Further information and important documentation can be found on the BASS documents page.

 EIT
 EIT Health’s Innovation Validation Call 2027 supports innovative digital and AI-powered medical technologies that are ready for real-world clinical validation and are approaching market launch. 
 This call addresses the funding gap for solutions that need to run clinical studies and collect evidence to demonstrate safety and efficacy, apply for regulatory approval and prepare for commercialisation. 
 Who can apply? 
 Consortia must comprise at least two organisations from different countries, representing at least two sides of the Knowledge Triangle (industry, research, education). A commercialising company must lead the project. Eligible solutions must be digital or AI-enabled medical devices (MDR/IVDR) at Innovation Maturity Level 6 (IML 6), aiming to reach IML 7 by project end.  Funding

 The commercialising entity must sign a Financial Sustainability Contribution Agreement and, if it is a micro or small enterprise, must receive €400,000–€500,000 of the grant.

 Solutions must have the potential to impact 150,000 patients or citizens in the EU and aim to be on the market and generating at least €10,000 in revenues within three years after the funding period.
